narr: A strong low pressure system moved across the southwestern U.S. on the 1st, delivering moderate to locally heavy rainfall activity as well as embedded thunderstorm activity. Moisture values were well above normal for early January, with Precipitable water values ranged between 0.8-1. There was also some instability present, with Mixed Layer CAPE values between 100-500 J/KG, resulting in the formation of thunderstorms. The combination of the favorable moisture and instability parameters along with the strong dynamical forcing from the low pressure system resulted in very favorable conditions for a widespread swath of moderate to locally heavy rainfall to affect most of south-central Arizona. Rainfall amounts on average were under an inch across the lower deserts, however, across the higher terrain amounts were significantly higher, between 1-3.
ev: Floodwater out of Whitlow Canyon led to the closure of Silver King Rd. The employee from Queen Valley Fire Department said it was the highest flow he has ever seen. A Pinal County Flood Control streamflow gauge on Queen Creek at El Camino Viejo measured peak flow around 7 feet. No damages or injuries were reported.
